The Delta State Government has imposed a curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area following reported violence at a campaign rally of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Uduere community, which allegedly left some people dead and others injured. The Delta State Police Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Public Relations Officer, SP Bright Edafe. According to the statement, the curfew will run from 6pm to 6am daily until further notice. The police said investigations had commenced to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible. The statement read, “Following the reported violence during a campaign rally of the NDC at Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, which allegedly resulted in loss of lives and injuries to several persons, the Delta State Government has imposed a curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area, from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily until further notice. The Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, was said to have directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order. Erale also ordered a full-scale investigation, assuring residents that anyone found culpable would face the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status. He extended condolences to the families of those who died and wished the injured a speedy recovery. Erale warned political actors and their supporters against thuggery, intimidation and the unlawful use of firearms, stressing that political differences should not degenerate into violence or loss of lives.
